sm: The conversation opens on drone warfare. The speakers say the Ukraine footage is horrifying, and they expect drones to get faster and more precise, even racing-style drones carrying bombs. Jocko Willink predicts a quick escalation to drone versus drone fighting, and says unmanned fighter jets will soon outperform human pilots. He adds that ground troops will still be needed to hold territory. They also look at a NASA quantum communications test that sent photons between an aircraft and a ground station. Asked about Iran, Willink says the lesson America keeps failing to learn is that outcomes can't be predicted. He compares war to an MMA fight or a bar fight, and says the US wrongly imposes its own thinking on other cultures. His example is Vietnam, where the US assumed a ten to one kill ratio would break the enemy, but it was Americans who lost the will to continue.

Willink continues that nobody can know whether Iran's will to fight will break, and that it is unclear who the enemy even is, the people or the regime. He says the situation now looks like modern siege warfare, with Iran isolated economically until it bargains, which he calls the best possible outcome. The hosts note they are recording in advance, and that reports of an attack on a US battleship were circulating, though unverified. Willink says the earlier Midnight Hammer strike made more sense because it didn't depend on Iran's reaction. A sustained campaign does depend on it, and that surprised him given the talk of no more foreign wars, which his generation backed after twenty years of war. He suggests the smooth Venezuela operation may have encouraged the decision. They agree the war was a major factor in the midterms because oil and prices rose and people lost faith in the decision-making.
